title: fix: update managed Codex catalog and protocol to 0.159.1
body:
Related: #161397

## What Problem This Solves

The managed Codex runtime still uses 0.158.0, whose bundled `model/list` catalog does not include GPT-6.1 Sol. Updating a separately installed CLI does not update the runtime selected by the official Codex plugin.

## Why This Change Was Made

Upgrade the managed CLI to [Codex 0.159.1](https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/tag/rust-v0.159.1), which adds GPT-6.1 Sol to its bundled catalog. Keep the managed version, ACP adapter override, OpenAI catalog client-version hint, native binary expectations, and generated dependency lock aligned. Refresh the harness documentation from the new runtime's actual `model/list` response and regenerate the protocol schemas so new terminal errors, including strict Guardian `tooManyDenials`, complete normally instead of timing out.

This complements #161400, which handles GPT-6.1 Sol provider metadata and request capabilities without changing the managed CLI dependency.

## User Impact

Accounts with access can discover GPT-6.1 Sol through the updated native runtime, including its advertised low, medium, high, xhigh, max, and ultra effort choices and priority/Fast tier. Full GPT-6.1 Sol routing also needs the provider metadata change in #161400; the CLI update alone does not supply those OpenClaw route facts. Catalog membership does not grant account access. Existing configured model selections and the external-runtime compatibility floor remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Direct, isolated app-server comparison using the official npm binaries and fresh unauthenticated homes: 0.158.0 returned 7 visible models and no `gpt-6.1-sol`; 0.159.1 returned 8, including `gpt-6.1-sol`, text/image input, all six efforts, and the priority/Fast tier. These are bundled-catalog observations, not account-entitlement or inference claims.
- Personally checked the release source at `openai/codex@8e68a98ef03cdde76d2e6800791ebdf1b3b95b24`: `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json`, `codex-rs/models-manager/src/manager.rs`, `codex-rs/app-server/src/models.rs`, and `codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/catalog_processor.rs`.
- 166 focused tests passed: managed dependency/ACP pin contracts, binary selection, app-server client/catalog, the shipped native model catalog, OpenAI provider discovery, and app-server fixture helpers. The final run used Node 24.19.0. An additional 55 protocol, turn-router, and run-attempt validation tests passed in 32.29 seconds across two shards. The new strict-Guardian router regression failed against the previous schemas and passes after regeneration; it uses fake timers and the existing in-memory client fixture (10 ms in the failing run). No new process fixtures were added.
- Generated all eight selected schemas with the official pinned binary and verified their normalized JSON against the experimental exports in the exact release source. Four compacted schema files changed. The Rust-based generator command was not run because Cargo is unavailable on this host.
- Fresh independent autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 findings after the schema fix.
- Frozen-lockfile installation, Codex and ACP npm lock validation, extension typechecking, scoped typed lint, dependency pin guard, formatting, docs MDX, internal links (14,626 checked, none broken), and `git diff --check` passed.
- The initial macOS authoring run did not run the Linux-only native-hook pressure E2E. The later same-host Linux comparison below closes that gap. Full repository CI remains a separate gate.

## Managed fresh-install and upgrade follow-up

Verified the earlier head `e29f0a3b8c29fc27e424e5c150db01cc7536404e` on macOS arm64 / Node 24.19.0 using isolated production dependency installations from the Codex plugin manifest. Only workspace development dependencies were omitted. The upgrade reused the same installation directory and Codex home, changing the managed dependency pin from 0.158.0 to 0.159.1 and running `npm install` again.

Each case used the real `setManagedCodexPluginRoot` → `resolveManagedCodexAppServerStartOptions` → `CodexAppServerClient.start` → `initialize` → `model/list` path, with package-only selection. There was no custom binary override, desktop fallback, mocked transport, or operator credential. The selected launcher was `node_modules/@openai/codex/bin/codex.js` under the isolated plugin installation.

| Case | Handshake version | Visible models | GPT-6.1 Sol | Existing config |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fresh managed install | 0.159.1 | 8 | Present | Preserved |
| Existing install before upgrade | 0.158.0 | 7 | Absent | Preserved |
| Same install after upgrade | 0.159.1 | 8 | Present | Preserved |

`config/read` retained `model_reasoning_effort=high`, the config file hash stayed unchanged, and every process closed successfully. This directly verifies managed package installation, selection, startup, and model discovery; it is not a full packaged `openclaw update` rehearsal, authenticated inference, or proof of account entitlement. No permanent test or CI cost was added for this one-off verification.

## Recovered Linux qualification and current landing status

The same isolated Linux arm64 runner completed both official managed binaries: 0.158.0 at baseline `cbc0a9d` and 0.159.1 at reviewed candidate `739dbad8820c47d3a24d2f494dba19a231b724fc`.

- All three native-hook pressure tests passed without skips for each version, covering six scenarios: matched 1/5/20-call execution, denied execution, unmatched policy, and no policy. Both versions had zero Gateway health errors and no leftover live or zombie relay processes. This is sampled compatibility evidence, not a statistical version-only performance claim; the baseline/candidate comparison also includes intervening main changes.
- Candidate Linux build passed. Focused discovery/cache/protocol checks passed 194 tests across six files in 101.65 seconds. A separate local focused run passed 227 tests across seven files, including warm reads, request deduplication, cache-key isolation and terminal-denial settlement.
- Independent API-backed review found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Both touched test files received whole-file audits; no blocking gaps or justified pruning were found. These results belong to the stated reviewed candidate, not a claim of passing newer-head CI.
- The isolated Linux container, source, dependencies, build output, private state and temporary managed binary installations were removed. No live Gateway update, model-selection change or authenticated inference is claimed by this qualification.

Previous head `b85dc7f2d88102369bb2193778fb4fb9cea26817` retained the reviewed 18-file PR delta after two main merges. [CI run 36751281606](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36751281606) finished with three failed shards, all in files untouched by this PR:

- Windows cancellation recovery: `update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts`, “restores Windows Scheduled Task autostart on SIGINT during package suspension”. The owning fix [#161990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161990) is merged at `05d3c90776e02dcf04044496a54652d6598b933a`.
- Gateway shutdown model-start race: `server-runtime-subscriptions.shutdown.test.ts`, “cancels auxiliary model work before inherited connection drain”. The owning fix [#162133](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162133) is merged at `22d7946296bfae995db08e02fce0694bf8f92b45`.
- Legacy listener socket lifetime: `plugin-legacy-listeners.test.ts`, three `EADDRINUSE` failures and one pooled-socket `UND_ERR_SOCKET`. The owning fix [4e4395c0d0f](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4e4395c0d0f13fce0ccad2443a777740bb37b306) is on main; it isolates the existing fork lane and uses fresh request connections.

### Published conflict-resolved candidate

Conflict-resolved head `1be1ac8557c7b07408a0f4cf84d8498b56b7aa85` incorporated main `db0aa867f24dfe2cc00e073d96f2580cb514dd87` and all three fixes above. The signed merge preserves contributor ancestry. Conflicts were limited to the Codex manifest, workspace overrides and lockfile: managed Codex remains 0.159.1 while main's fs-safe/CodeMirror dependency changes are preserved. The final PR delta is 18 files, +120/−66; no unrelated production or test changes were authored.

- Final-candidate focused proof: **200 tests passed across 8 files / 5 shards in 121.42 seconds**, covering OpenAI provider/discovery, live SDK catalog and strict boundaries, prepared-model catalog, Codex lifecycle, Gateway shutdown and legacy listeners.
- Fresh API-backed independent review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Both PR-touched test files are unchanged from their earlier complete-file audits; no distinct coverage was pruned.
- Pinned pnpm frozen install passed using the canonical global store. The actual managed binary reports `codex-cli 0.159.1`. Dependency pin guard (708 specs / 196 manifests), protocol coverage (65 events), scoped formatting, PR-delta whitespace check and Codex/ACP npm lock validation passed.
- [CI run 36932249733](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36932249733) subsequently exposed one real-Gateway UI readiness failure; the correction below addresses it. Dependency review passed and ClawSweeper completed this revision with no introduced findings. Neither result waives fresh checks after a push.

### CI readiness correction

Intermediate head `c672222f974fad8a29a413190da2b72e62823618` added a single test-only correction in `model-catalog-partial-refresh.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (+2/−1). The existing assertion checked effort enablement immediately after visibility. The model menu intentionally becomes usable before initial chat history has finished loading, while effort remains disabled during that loading phase.

- Reproduced the exact CI assertion failure locally on unchanged `1be1ac8`; the captured screenshot shows the chat-loading skeleton. Awaiting `aria-disabled=false` with the existing default polling timeout makes the same isolated real-Gateway test pass (one test covering both new and existing chat routes, 26.56 seconds). No production code, expected outcome, assertion strength or timeout was changed.
- A fresh API-backed review audited the full test file, fixture/cleanup, socket discovery, both routes and production readiness owner. No P0–P2 finding or justified pruning. The original two touched-test audits remain applicable; their files are unchanged.
- Focused lint, formatting and 14 changed-file guards passed. The combined local check then stopped at the TypeScript graph boundary because it rejects the canonical global pnpm store as outside the checkout. No guard bypass or duplicate dependency graph was used; remaining type checks must pass in exact-head GitHub CI under its standard dependency layout.
- Fresh head-bound dependency approval, ClawSweeper and CI remain required. No current-head CI success, merge or live Gateway deployment is claimed.

### Reconciled candidate before final CI repair

Head `67b7e2fe8bf7edd82b383080bc7d155b3cb73d78` incorporates main `2f4808320cf81e6361b9bedd502aa1b9ec1b7ca7`. Main independently landed the same UI readiness correction in [#162869](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162869) while the failure was being reproduced. That test was the only merge conflict; this candidate retains main's exact file, so there is no additional UI test delta in this PR.

The PR is again **18 files, +120/−66**. Every per-file added/removed-line delta matches reviewed `1be1ac8`, and both original touched-test file blobs are unchanged. The lock merged automatically, preserving main's Undici 8.11.2. Frozen installation passed using the shared canonical store.

Focused requalification on the reconciled tree passed **209 tests across eight files / four shards in 79.54 seconds**: live SDK catalog (62), prepared model catalog (36), Codex lifecycle/new main request diagnostics/native projection (46), and OpenAI provider/discovery (65). Prior independent review, whole-file audits and accurately head-bound Linux evidence remain applicable to the unchanged upgrade delta. Fresh exact-head GitHub CI, ClawSweeper completion and dependency approval remain required; the local typecheck layout limitation above is not a waiver.


### Current candidate: registration-safe timeout diagnostics

Head `c730632d7d64aeafae271785c7d752d976392a1c` adds one necessary, one-line correction to inherited main code. [CI job 110613579798](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36934946316/job/110613579798) failed the existing Codex registration import-boundary test: main's new `request-diagnostics.ts` imported the broad agent runtime SDK, introducing ten paths to live config/session/runtime modules. The helper now imports the **same logger binding** from the existing lightweight registration SDK. No logging behavior, tests, assertions or timeouts are changed. Original upgrade delta remains unchanged; total scope is 19 files, +121/−67.

- Reproduced the exact boundary failure locally on unchanged `67b7e2f`: one failed/two passed. After correction, **60 tests in three files passed in 20.46 seconds**, covering registration, request lifecycle and timeout diagnostics, including redaction, cancellation, retry, cleanup and throwing sinks. Prior 209-test requalification remains bound to `67b7e2f`; the new run covers the corrected owner and affected siblings.
- Fresh API-backed independent review: scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Existing test files are unchanged; prior whole-file audits still apply. Scoped lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- Local `pnpm build` reaches `tsdown-ai` then fails because declaration tooling rejects TypeScript in the canonical shared pnpm store as outside the checkout. This is the same concrete layout limitation as the earlier local type check. No guard bypass or duplicate dependency graph was used. Exact-head hosted build, type, lint and test checks remain mandatory.
- The earlier accepted auto-merge was explicitly cancelled through native recovery before publishing this correction. Current-head dependency approval, ClawSweeper completion and CI are required before native replacement recovery. No CI waiver, completed merge or live Gateway deployment is claimed.
